rows.english: Here we will analyze the statement [from Entering the Middle Way, by Master Chandrakirti (650 AD)] where it says, "...The mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus." One may begin with the following question: Let's consider the objects of the following states of mind: the visual consciousness of a craving spirit where a river of water looks like pus and blood; the visual consciousness of a person with a kind of cataract where a clean white porcelain basin looks like a hair has fallen into it; and that kind of meditation where you visualize skeletons--where you imagine that the entire surface of the earth is covered with the bones of corpses. Are all these objects completely equivalent, as far as being something that exists or doesn't exist?

rows.acip: KHA CIG NA RE, RGYU MTSAN DE NYID KYI PHYIR NA, CHOS THAMS CAD LA 'DI YIN 'DI MIN GANG DU YANG BZUNG DU MED DO, , ZHES ZER NA, SANGS RGYAS PA'I GRUB MTHA' DANG , PHYI ROL PA'I GRUB MTHA' LA BZANG NGAN DANG , BDAG CAG GI STON PA DANG , PHYI ROL PA'I STON PA LA MCHOG DMAN SOGS MED PAR THAL,
rows.wylie: kha cig na re, rgyu mtshan de nyid kyi phyir na, chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med do, , zhes zer na, sangs rgyas pa'i grub mtha' dang , phyi rol pa'i grub mtha' la bzang ngan dang , bdag cag gi ston pa dang , phyi rol pa'i ston pa la mchog dman sogs med par thal
rows.english: Someone may make the following claim: Given the statements that have come above, the fact is that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Well then, you must be suggesting that the system of the Buddha is all the same as the system of every non-Buddhist belief, that there is no difference in their correctness at all. And you must be saying too that we could never state that our Teacher was the highest teacher, and that the teachers of the non- Buddhists are lesser.

rows.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD LA 'DI YIN 'DI MIN GANG DU YANG BZUNG DU MED PA'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA, YOD PAR THAL, BDAG NI STON PA GZHAN SPANGS NAS, , KHYOD LA SKYABS SU MCHI LAGS KYI, , CI SLAD CE NA KHYED NYID NI, , SKYON MI MNGA' ZHING YON TAN RDZOGS, , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med pa'i phyir, 'dod na, yod par thal, bdag ni ston pa gzhan spangs nas, , khyod la skyabs su mchi lags kyi, , ci slad ce na khyed nyid ni, , skyon mi mnga' zhing yon tan rdzogs, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: And you must be suggesting all this, for you have claimed that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Now if you should agree that none of the differences mentioned above exist, we must reply that they do, for as the verse says: All other teachers now I've given up, And go for refuge now to only You; Why? Because it's You alone who has No fault, and perfected every good.

rows.wylie: kha cig na re, rgyu mtshan de nyid kyi phyir na, chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med do, , zhes zer na, sangs rgyas pa'i grub mtha' dang , phyi rol pa'i grub mtha' la bzang ngan dang , bdag cag gi ston pa dang , phyi rol pa'i ston pa la mchog dman sogs med par thal
rows.english: Someone may make the following claim: Given the statements that have come above, the fact is that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Well then, you must be suggesting that the system of the Buddha is all the same as the system of every non-Buddhist belief, that there is no difference in their correctness at all. And you must be saying too that we could never state that our Teacher was the highest teacher, and that the teachers of the non- Buddhists are lesser.

rows.wylie: chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med pa'i phyir, 'dod na, yod par thal, bdag ni ston pa gzhan spangs nas, , khyod la skyabs su mchi lags kyi, , ci slad ce na khyed nyid ni, , skyon mi mnga' zhing yon tan rdzogs, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: And you must be suggesting all this, for you have claimed that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Because it's You alone who has No fault, and perfected every good.

rows.acip: DES NA, LAS CAN GYI 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, TSAD MTSUNGS NGES PAR DGOS PA MA YIN TE, DGOS NA, PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I NANG DU GNAS KYI BLOS GNAS SHING , THA MAL GYI MIG SHES KYIS MI BZOD PA'I SROG CHAGS PHRA MO'I MIG SHES KYIS KYANG , DE'I TSAD MAR 'GRO DGOS PA DANG , RGYA MTSO'I NANG NA GNAS PA'I SROG CHAGS PHRA MO'I MIG SHES KYIS KYANG , RGYA MTSO'I TSAD LA TSAD MAR 'GRO DGOS PA DANG , LHA MA YIN 'GA' ZHIG LA, MTSON CHA PHOR GANG SNANG DGOS PA LA SOGS PA'I SKYON YOD PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: des na, las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, tshad mtshungs nges par dgos pa ma yin te, dgos na, phor pa gang po de'i nang du gnas kyi blos gnas shing , tha mal gyi mig shes kyis mi bzod pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , de'i tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , rgya mtsho'i nang na gnas pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , rgya mtsho'i tshad la tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , lha ma yin 'ga' zhig la, mtshon cha phor gang snang dgos pa la sogs pa'i skyon yod pa'i phyir
rows.english: In conclusion now, let us consider again these three kinds of beings, each with their different karma, as they sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It's not necessarily true that they must all have valid perceptions which are identical. If they did, then the three beings looking at the glass of water would have to think of the water as a place to live, in the way that a creature living in water would. The three beings as well would have to see the water in the same way that microscopic organisms living in the water, little beings imperceptible to normal visual consciousness, see it with their own visual consciousness. Then too the visual consciousness of microscopic organisms living in the depths of the ocean would have to be a valid perception towards the entire extent of the sea. And certain kinds of near-gods too would have to see weapons as glasses of water, and on and on; the problems raised would be many.

rows.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

rows.english: The one-day vows are called "staying close" because they help you stay close to nirvana in the sense of taking you there. The lifetime vows for laymen and laywomen are called "close to virtue" because they help you be close to virtue, which here refers to nirvana. The vows of male novices and female novices are called "way to virtue" because those who possess these vows have entered the way, that is the path, which leads to virtue, again referring to nirvana. The vows of an intermediate nun are called "versed in virtue" because these women are versing themselves in the twelve rules, in order to be able to keep the vows of a fully ordained nun. Fully ordained monks and fully ordained nuns are called "begging for virtue" because they are begging, that is seeking, that state of virtue: nirvana. In this verse Je Tsongkapa is thus listing the eight kinds of individual freedom vows. 31 The Asian Classics Institute Course IX: The Ethical Life Reading Four: A General Description of the Vows, Part One The following selection consists of the second major section of Daymaker (Nyin- byed), composed by Master Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra (1772-1851) as a commentary to the Essence of the Ocean of Discipline ('Dul-ba rgya-mtso'i snying- po), a summary of the vinaya teachings by Je Tsongkapa (1357-1419). ************

rows.english: The one-day vows are called "staying close" because they help you stay close to nirvana in the sense of taking you there. The lifetime vows for laymen and laywomen are called "close to virtue" because they help you be close to virtue, which here refers to nirvana. The vows of male novices and female novices are called "way to virtue" because those who possess these vows have entered the way, that is the path, which leads to virtue, again referring to nirvana. The vows of an intermediate nun are called "versed in virtue" because these women are versing themselves in the twelve rules, in order to be able to keep the vows of a fully ordained nun. Fully ordained monks and fully ordained nuns are called "begging for virtue" because they are begging, that is seeking, that state of virtue: nirvana. In this verse Je Tsongkapa is thus listing the eight kinds of individual freedom vows. 6 The Root Four One-Day Vows

rows.english: This brings us to the second division in this portion of the text: an explanation of bringing our consciousness to "enter" the "city" of another's body.  The custom of referring to the eyes and other sense organs as "the village," and to the bases of these powers as "the city," is something that has come from the teachings on the perfection of wisdom.  The body of another person who has died--a body which is still fresh and has not deteriorated--is also referred to here as a "city." rows.english: Suppose, moreover, that a deep practitioner has gone into a state of meditative focus. rows.acip: RANG YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS SPYI BO NAS MGRIN PAR SLEB PA NA DGA' BA, MGRIN PA NAS SNYING GAR SLEB PA NA MCHOG DGA', SNYING GNAS LTE BAR SLEB PA NA KHYAD DGA', LTE BA NAS GSANG GNAS KYI RTZER SLEB PA NA LHAN CIG SKYES BA'I DGA' BA SKYES, BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA NI DBANG GSUM BA'I NGO BO YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: rang yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i byang chub kyi sems spyi bo nas mgrin par sleb pa na dga' ba, mgrin pa nas snying gar sleb pa na mchog dga', snying gnas lte bar sleb pa na khyad dga', lte ba nas gsang gnas kyi rtser sleb pa na lhan cig skyes ba'i dga' ba skyes, bde stong dbyer med kyi lhan skyes kyi dga' ba ni dbang gsum ba'i ngo bo yin no
rows.english: (Speak then to the disciple these words, so they understand what is happening:) The two of you, The Man and Woman, Go into union. The Wish for enlightenment Flows from the top of your heads To your throats, Bringing you ecstasy. From your throats then It flows to your hearts, Bringing you high ecstasy. Flowing from your hearts To your navels, It brings you incredible ecstasy. From your navels it flows To the tips of your secret places, Bringing you simultaneous bliss. And it is this simultaneous bliss, Indivisible ecstasy and voidness, Which is the true essence Of this, the third initiation.

rows.english: (At this point, one either experiences, directly, the wisdom of bliss and voidness which comes through the practice of union--or else one only imagines they have experienced it.  One experiences great bliss, or else only imagines that they have.  Be sure to acquaint the disciple with these and the other possibilities that occur during the empowerment; let them know that there are different ways in which one may be granted this Initiation of Infinite Wisdom. And then take off their blindfold.) 100) The purity which is granted

rows.acip: ZHABS GA-YAS BSKUMS SHING GA-YON BRKYANGS PA'I STABS KYIS BZHUGS PA, YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA'I THUGS KA'I H'Um GI 'OD ZER GYIS BKUG PA'I KHRO BO BCU ZHAL DU BCUG NAS ZHU BA RDO RJE'I LAM NAS YUM GYI PADMAR ZHUGS PA'I THIG LE BCU LAS H'Um RING PO BCU DANG DE LAS KHRO BO BCUR GYUR,
rows.wylie: zhabs ga-yas bskums shing ga-yon brkyangs pa'i stabs kyis bzhugs pa, yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i thugs ka'i hUM gi 'od zer gyis bkug pa'i khro bo bcu zhal du bcug nas zhu ba rdo rje'i lam nas yum gyi padmar zhugs pa'i thig le bcu las hUM ring po bcu dang de las khro bo bcur gyur
rows.english: I am standing with my right leg bent And my left leg extended. As Husband and Wife we join together in meditation, And from the hung at our precious heart Come rays of light Which bring down the ten Wrathful Ones. They enter my mouth and melt. They reach my diamond inside her lotus, And from her lotus come ten drops, And from the drops ten long hung letters. These transform into the Ten Wrathful Ones.

rows.acip: MAN SNYER NYER SPYOD LNGA PHYI'I MCHOD PA DANG BSGOMS PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR LA RANG GI SA BON LA SOGS PA 'DZIN PA RNAMS KYIS MCHOD PA GSANG PA'I MCHOD PA DANG YUM DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS DGA' BA BZHI'I RIMS KYIS NYON MONGS DAG PA'I GO 'PHANG MNGON DU BYAS PA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA DANG ,
rows.wylie: man snyer nyer spyod lnga phyi'i mchod pa dang bsgoms pa'i dkyil 'khor la rang gi sa bon la sogs pa 'dzin pa rnams kyis mchod pa gsang pa'i mchod pa dang yum dang snyoms par zhugs pas dga' ba bzhi'i rims kyis nyon mongs dag pa'i go 'phang mngon du byas pa de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa dang
rows.english: The Golden Harvest explains these offerings as follows.  The outer offering consists of the offering of the five objects of enjoyment: the objects of the senses.  The secret offering is where we make offerings to the beings of a secret world which we are meditating upon, utilizing things that are subsumed within ourselves, such as our seed. The offering of suchness is where we go into union with a consort and experience the four levels of bliss, one by one, and thus actualize the state free of mental afflictions.

rows.wylie: rnal 'byor rgyud ltar na, slob dpon shAkya bshes gnyen dang sangs rgyas gsang ba gnyis kyis rgyal po gzhon nu don grub chu bo ni rany+dza na'i 'gram du rab mtha'i bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par zhugs pa'i tshe, phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyis se gol gyi sgras bslangs te bskul nas 'og min du khrid de
rows.english: How does the class of deep practice explain this point?  The masters Shakyamitra and Buddhaguhya both say that Prince Siddhartha went into deep meditation on the fourth concentration level, at the very limit, sitting on the banks of the Ranjana River.  All the Buddhas in every corner of the universe then snapped Their fingers; and the sound brought him up out of this meditation and urged him higher.

rows.acip: DES NA SLOB DPON KUN DGA' SNYING POS, STON PA 'DI BSKAL PA GRANGS MED GSUM DU TSOGS BSAGS NAS SRID PA THA MAR GYUR PA'I TSE, 'OG MIN DU RAB MTHA'I BSAM GTAN BZHI PA LA SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA NA, PHYOGS BCU'I SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYIS SE GOL GYI SGRAS BSLANGS PA SOGS SU BSHAD PA LTAR 'DOD DGOS TE,
rows.wylie: des na slob dpon kun dga' snying pos, ston pa 'di bskal pa grangs med gsum du tshogs bsags nas srid pa tha mar gyur pa'i tshe, 'og min du rab mtha'i bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par zhugs pa na, phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyis se gol gyi sgras bslangs pa sogs su bshad pa ltar 'dod dgos te
rows.english: As such, we would have to accept the position expressed by the master Anandagarbha.  His explanation begins by saying that our Teacher spent three countless masses of eons collecting good deeds.  Then, when he was about to reach the end of the cycle of pain, he went into deep meditation on the fourth concentration level, at the very limit, within the Heaven Below None.  At this point all the Buddhas in every corner of the universe snapped Their fingers, and the sound brought him up out of the meditation, and so on.

rows.acip: GSANG BA'I SNA RTZER RDZAS THIG BSGOM PA NI, RANG DANG LAS RGYA GNYIS SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LAS BYANG SEMS DH'U T'I'I MAR SNA GNYIS 'PHRAD MTSAMS SU 'PHO MED DU 'DZIN PA DANG , RANG DANG YE RGYA'I DH'U T'I'I MAR SNA GNYIS 'PHRAD MTSAMS SU THIG LE LA DMIGS NAS BSGOM PA GNYIS YOD DO,,
rows.wylie: gsang ba'i sna rtser rdzas thig bsgom pa ni, rang dang las rgya gnyis snyoms par zhugs pa las byang sems dhU tI'i mar sna gnyis 'phrad mtshams su 'pho med du 'dzin pa dang , rang dang ye rgya'i dhU tI'i mar sna gnyis 'phrad mtshams su thig le la dmigs nas bsgom pa gnyis yod do
rows.english: There are two ways in which we practice with a drop of substance at the opening of the secret channel.  For the first, we go into the meditation with a partner of the rite; when the element comes, then we hold it, without letting it move, at the juncture where the two lower openings of the channels of dance are touching.  For the second, we meditate, focusing on the drop at the juncture where the two channels of dance--those of ourselves and of our partner of the rite--are touching.

For the second, we meditate, focusing on the drop at the juncture where the two channels of dance--those of ourselves and of our partner of the rite--are touching."}

rows.acip: DE GNYIS KYI GSANG DBANG NI RIM BZHIN BLA MAS RIG MA GCIG DANG DGU DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I GSANG RDZAS MYANGS PA DANG , RIG MA GCIG DANG DGU'I BHA GA BLTAS PA LAS SKYES PA'I BDE BA LA MDZAD DE, BHA GA'I DKYIL 'KHOR DU THOB PA ZHES BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: de gnyis kyi gsang dbang ni rim bzhin bla mas rig ma gcig dang dgu dang snyoms par zhugs pa las byung ba'i gsang rdzas myangs pa dang , rig ma gcig dang dgu'i bha ga bltas pa las skyes pa'i bde ba la mdzad de, bha ga'i dkyil 'khor du thob pa zhes bya'o
rows.english: The secret empowerment for these two refers, respectively, to the following.  The Lama goes into union with either one, or nine, Women of Knowledge; and then we partake of the secret substance which comes from this union.  And there is also the pleasure that we feel as we gaze upon the bhaga of either one, or nine, Women of Knowledge.  This empowerment then is said to be "attained in the secret world of the bhaga."

rows.wylie: de nas, bla ma rdo rje rnal 'byor ma dang kha TvaM ga 'khor lo sdom par gyur pa snyoms par zhugs pa'i byang sems dkar dmar aoM gsum ma la 'bru gsum btags pa dang , g-yon pa'i mtheb srin gyis thod pa'i bdud rtsi myangs la, zhes lcer bzhag pa myangs pas
rows.english: (Continue on with:) The khatvanga staff Of your Lama, The Angel of Diamond, Transforms into the Angel Of the Union of Spheres, And We go into The meditation of union. We speak the Mantra of the Triple Om, Embellished by the three letters, Over the white and red Elements of Enlightenment. With the thumb and ring finger Of your left hand, You partake of the nectar Of deathlessness, Lifting it from The cup of skull. (Place some nectar upon the initiates tongue, and have them partake of it.)

rows.wylie: rang nyid rdo rje rnal 'byor ma dang bla ma rje btsun mas gtad pa'i 'khor lo sdom pa snyoms par zhugs pa'i byang sems gsang gnas nas lte bar slebs pa na dga' ba, lte ba nas snying gar slebs pa na mchog dga', snying ga nas mgrin par slebs pa na khyad dga', mgrin pa nas spyi bor slebs pa na
rows.english: (See now the following:) I myself Am the Angel of Diamond; And the Angel, Who is my Lama, Passes over to me The Angel of the Union Of the Spheres. We sit in the meditation Of union. The element of Enlightenment Begins to flow upwards Inside of Us, From the place of the secret. When it reaches the navel, We have ecstasy. When it flows from the navel And reaches the heart, We have high ecstasy. When it flows from the heart And reaches the throat, We have incredible ecstasy. And then it flows From the throat To the tip of Our head:

rows.wylie: (gis nang mchod 'bul, rang gi thugs ka nas padma can la sogs pa'i rig ma dpag tu med pa spros pa rnams rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i skur gyur pa dang bla ma yab yum snyoms par zhugs pas zag med kyi bde bas khyab par bsams la,)

rows.acip: YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS BYANG SEMS ZHU BA SPYI BO NAS MGRIN PAR SLEB PA NA DGA' BA, MGRIN PA NAS SNYING GAR SLEB PA NA MCHOG DGA', SNYING GNAS LTE BAR SLEB PA NA KHYAD DGA', LTE BA NAS NOR BU'I RTZER SLEB PA NA LHAN SKYES KYI YE SHES SKYES PAS BDE BA DANG STONG PA NYID DBYER MED PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN LA SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS,
rows.wylie: yab yum snyoms par zhugs pas byang sems zhu ba spyi bo nas mgrin par sleb pa na dga' ba, mgrin pa nas snying gar sleb pa na mchog dga', snying gnas lte bar sleb pa na khyad dga', lte ba nas nor bu'i rtser sleb pa na lhan skyes kyi ye shes skyes pas bde ba dang stong pa nyid dbyer med pa'i ting nge 'dzin la snyoms par zhugs
rows.english: The Man and Wife Sit in meditation, Which makes the Bodhi minds melt. It starts to flow down inside From the tip of Our heads; When it reaches the throat, We have Ecstasy. When it flows from the throat And reaches the heart, We have High Ecstasy. When it flows from the heart And reaches the navel, We have Incredible Ecstasy. When it flows from the navel And reaches the tip of the jewel, We have simultaneous wisdom, Which lets us sit together In meditation, our minds Fixed single-pointedly On indivisible Bliss and emptiness.

rows.acip: DE LTA BU'I RIG MA PHUL BA DE DAG RNAL 'BYOR MAR GYUR PA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS ZAG MED KYI BDE BA THUGS RGYUD LA 'KHRUNGS PAR BSAMS PA GSANG BA SHER DBANG DANG 'BREL BA'I MCHOD PA DANG,

rows.english: Imagine that, when you offer these Enlightened Women, They each turn into the Angel herself, and sit in meditation of union with the Lamas.  This makes immaculate bliss rise up in Their hearts; and thus you have made the secret offering, the one that relates to the empowerment of wisdom.

rows.acip: BAm YIG NANG GI RDO RJE BTZUN MO'I MCHOG ,CES PA'I DON PHYI'I LAS RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS NANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I BTZUN MO KHAMS DMAR PO ME'I RANG BZHIN DE SBAR BA LA BRTEN NAS SPYI BO'I KHAMS DKAR PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA DE ZHU, DE GNYIS SNYING KHAR 'DU 'PHROD BYAS PAS NA DE LTA BU'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I RTZE DGAS ROL BAR ZHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: baM yig nang gi rdo rje btsun mo'i mchog ,ces pa'i don phyi'i las rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la brten nas phyag rgya'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas nang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i btsun mo khams dmar po me'i rang bzhin de sbar ba la brten nas spyi bo'i khams dkar po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa de zhu, de gnyis snying khar 'du 'phrod byas pas na de lta bu'i rang zhal mthong ba'i rtse dgas rol bar zhog ces pa dang
rows.english: The next line of His prayer, which mentions "the inner Angel, Supreme Queen of Diamond, the sacred sound of vam," refers to the following process.  When you enjoy union with your outer partner of ritual, a wind comes from Her secret place, like a stream of smoke from a stick of incense.  This forces the downward-clearing wind within your own body to reverse direction and come up. This then causes the Queen at your navel (the red element, which is of the nature of fire) to blaze.  This blazing in turn causes the white element at the tip of your head (which is of the nature of Heruka) to melt down.  And then these two elements come together and collide at the heart.  What Master Tsarchen is praying for then is that He might laugh and play in the bliss of seeing the Angel's true face in this sense.

rows.wylie: de nas dbang lha bzhugs bzhugs pa byas nas bla ma yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i byang sems lcer bzhag pa myangs pas gsang dbang thob par mos
rows.english: Then you can see yourself taking a secret empowerment here as well.  The Angels of Empowerment linger, and the Lama Man and Wife go into the meditation of union. rows.acip: BZHI PA LA GSUM, RIG MA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS BSKYED PA'I BDUD RTZI ZOS PA'I BCUD LEN GYIS LUS KYI STOBS RGYAS PAR BYA BA, GSUNG RDO RJE'I LCES RTZA BSKUL NAS BDE BA BSKYED DE LAS BYUNG BA'I BDUD RTZI LCES MYANG BA DANG, PADMA CAN LA SOGS PA'I PHYAG RGYA RNAMS KYIS YID DGA' BAR BYA ZHING DE RNAMS KYI THUGS SUN MI DBYUNG PA MJUG SDUD DANG BCAS PA'O,,

rows.english: The fourth topic has three parts: (1) A description of how we partake of the nectar that is produced when we engage in union with our Lady of Knowledge, and how this acts as a nutritive essence which strengthens the body; (2) How we use our tongue--as the diamond of enlightened speech--to stimulate the lower end of the partner's inner channel, and produce bliss in Her; and then use our tongue again to partake of the nectar that comes from Her because of this bliss; (3) How partners such as the Lady of the Lotus are pleased, and how we must be careful never to upset their minds--along with a concluding section. * * * Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) gives some additional, useful detail on the need for both inner and outer aids in his Book to Please Those with a Core of Goodness: A Brief Explanation of the Very Essence of "The Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps," on the Stage of Completion in the Teachings of the Glorious Secret Collection (ACIP digital text S00260, ff. 26b-27a):

rows.acip: DE LA 'DIR PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS SROG RTZOL DU 'GRO BA'I TSUL, ZHES PA DA LTAR GYI GANG ZAG LA DNGOS SU MI DGOS PA SHAS CHE YANG, DE'I GO BA CHAGS NA BSKYED RIM SGOM BA SOGS KYI SKABS SU, YE RGYA LA BRTEN PA LA PHAN CHE BAS NYE BAR MKHO BA YIN NO,,

rows.english: We come to a point in the text then where it talks about "how we turn union with an actual, outside partner into a practice for the control of the inner winds."  Most people nowadays aren't to the point where they would actually need this, but it is useful to gain some understanding of it.  And so at junctures such as where you are practicing the stage of creation, it can be very helpful to utilize an imaginary partner--we can even say it is a necessity. * * * The points at which we practice with the two partners are identified by Je Rinpoche in His commentary to Highest Bliss (Sanvara) entitled An Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316, folio 123b).

And so at junctures such as where you are practicing the stage of creation, it can be very helpful to utilize an imaginary partner--we can even say it is a necessity. * * * The points at which we practice with the two partners are identified by Je Rinpoche in His commentary to Highest Bliss (Sanvara) entitled An Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316, folio 123b)."}

rows.acip: SEMS BRTAN (YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA SEMS BRTAN PA MED PA RNAMS KYIS, PA TSAB CHAG PHYI ROL GYI ZER, KHA CIG CHAG 'GYUR GYI DE MI 'THAD DE, RGYA DPE LA DGAG SGRA GSAL BAR MED CING, 'GREL PAR SEMS BRTAN PA ZHES BSHAD PA DANG 'GAL BAS SO, ,ZHES PA DE NI MI 'THAD DE, 'GREL PAR SEMS BRTAN PA ZHES PA'I 'GYUR BTZAS PA YIN PAS GNOD BYED DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR DANG,
rows.wylie: sems brtan (ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la sems brtan pa med pa rnams kyis, pa tshab chag phyi rol gyi zer, kha cig chag 'gyur gyi de mi 'thad de, rgya dpe la dgag sgra gsal bar med cing, 'grel par sems brtan pa zhes bshad pa dang 'gal bas so, ,zhes pa de ni mi 'thad de, 'grel par sems brtan pa zhes pa'i 'gyur btsas pa yin pas gnod byed du mi rung ba'i phyir dang
rows.english: When their understanding has thus become firm, they can engage in union with an outer partner.  This will bring them, the coming lines indicate, the experience of highest bliss.  (Where the text here mentions "what is done by those who do not have a firm understanding of the practice of union with an imaginary partner," we see in the translations of Patsab and Chak "an outer partner."  Some have said that Chak's translation is incorrect, since the original Sanskrit manuscript includes no clear negative grammar particle here, and because it contradicts the commentary, which at this point says "those who do have a firm understanding."  This position though is itself incorrect, since the mention of "those of firm understanding" in the commentary is using twilight language, and is thus inappropriate to use as a line to refute some other position.)

rows.acip: 'DI LA BSKYED RIM PAS NI SPROS PA GZHAN 'DOR MOD KYANG, CHO GA'I RIM PA NI 'DRA BAR MNGON PAS, DKYIL 'KHOR RGYAL MCHOG RDZOGS PA DANG YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS TE, DGA' BZHI'I RIM GYIS LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA BSKYED DE BDE STONG SGOM MO,,

rows.english: Now it is true that in this regard a practitioner on the stage of creation gives up other kinds of elaboration; but it would seem to me that the steps of their ritual would be similar to what we've been describing.  And so they could perform the practice of the Supreme Victor of the Secret World, and engage in union with an imaginary partner, and thus bring on the four blisses.  With this then they would in stages reach the  simultaneous form of bliss, and then could meditate on bliss and voidness.

rows.english: In the three different contexts of the practice of the stage of completion then you would take some step of the ritual that involved going into union with an imaginary partner.  You thus perfect a deep practice of working with the inner winds which then lends you support in the task of eliminating a great many forms of elaboration, in the sense of perceiving things in duality.  And then you would manifest an extraordinary form of the four forms of emptiness.

rows.acip: BAm YIG NANG GI RDO RJE BTZUN MO'I MCHOG ,CES PA'I DON PHYI'I LAS RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS NANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I BTZUN MO KHAMS DMAR PO ME'I RANG BZHIN DE SBAR BA LA BRTEN NAS SPYI BO'I KHAMS DKAR PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA DE ZHU, DE GNYIS SNYING KHAR 'DU 'PHROD BYAS PAS NA DE LTA BU'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I RTZE DGAS ROL PAR ZHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: baM yig nang gi rdo rje btsun mo'i mchog ,ces pa'i don phyi'i las rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la brten nas phyag rgya'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas nang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i btsun mo khams dmar po me'i rang bzhin de sbar ba la brten nas spyi bo'i khams dkar po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa de zhu, de gnyis snying khar 'du 'phrod byas pas na de lta bu'i rang zhal mthong ba'i rtse dgas rol par zhog ces pa dang
rows.english: The next line of His prayer, which mentions "the inner Angel, Supreme Queen of Diamond, the sacred sound of vam," refers to the following process.  When you enjoy union with your actual, outer partner, a wind comes from Her secret place, like a stream of smoke from a stick of incense.  This forces the downward-clearing wind within your own body to reverse direction and come up. This then causes the Queen at your navel (the red element, which is of the nature of fire) to blaze.  This blazing in turn causes the white element at the tip of your head (which is of the nature of Heruka) to melt down.  And then these two elements come together and collide at the heart.  What Master Tsarchen is praying for then is that He might laugh and play in the bliss of seeing the Angel's true face in this sense.

rows.acip: SNANG BA GSAL BA DANG DE BRTAN PA RNYED NA, DE DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS NAS DGA' BZHI BSKYED PA'I LHAN SKYES KYI DUS SU, BDE STONG SBYOR NUS NA LTA BA DRAN PAR BYAS LA BDE STONG DBYER MED DU BSKYANG,
rows.wylie: snang ba gsal ba dang de brtan pa rnyed na, de dang snyoms par zhugs nas dga' bzhi bskyed pa'i lhan skyes kyi dus su, bde stong sbyor nus na lta ba dran par byas la bde stong dbyer med du bskyang
rows.english: If they keep this up over a long period of time, then they will reach a point where their visualization is very clear, and firm.  They go into union with this partner, and attain the point of the simultaneous, where they are able to bring on the four forms of bliss.  If you are able thus to achieve a union of bliss and emptiness, then try to bring to mind the correct view of reality, and maintain this vision of indivisible bliss and voidness.

rows.english: And then the Man and the Woman go into union.  The element of enlightenment reaches the tip of the diamond rod, and we learn to identify just which of the blisses is coming to us. rows.english: The Golden Harvest explains these offerings as follows.  The outer offering consists of the offering of the five objects of enjoyment: the objects of the senses.  The secret offering is where we make offerings to the Beings of a secret world which we are meditating upon, utilizing things that are subsumed within ourselves, such as our seed. rows.english: In His hands He holds a diamond and bell which are symbols, meant to represent something else, and He embraces--as His holy Wife--the Diamond Queen of the Empty Realm.  He is enjoying His play in the bliss and void where, when the Man and Woman go into union, They experience the pleasure of an indivisible union of simultaneous bliss and an emptiness of any inherent nature.

rows.wylie: mi rnams kyis ni mngar ba dang dvangs pa dang bsil ba'i chur rtog cing khrus byed do, ,'thung ngo der 'jug go ,nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched la snyoms par zhugs pa'i lha rnams kyis ni nam mkhar mthong ste, gzugs kyi 'du shes rnam par bshig pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad do

rows.english: It happened one day In a moment of mental clarity-- I was thinking a bit On the essence of all the teachings I'd heard, And the thought Made my think of all the kindness That my Lama Had ever paid to me. And then I blurted out this Song of the Diamond, Which is meant To repay in some small way My Lord, My Lama, for all his kindness, Taking everything That I've gleaned from the years Of scripture, And whispered advice, and logic, And expressing it all In that extraordinary method Where you take the goal And use it as the path to the goal.

rows.acip: RANG BZHIN GYI GNAS 'OG MIN NI CHOS SKU LA SOGS PA RANG GI NYE LOGS KYI NAM MKHA' NAS, NAM MKHA' DVANGS PA LAS SPRIN BLO BUR DU LDANG BA LTAR PHYOGS BCU'I RGYAL BA THAMS CAD DPAL RDO RJE 'JIGS BYED KYI RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI RNAM PA DPAG TU MED PAR SPYAN DRANGS NAS MA MTHA' DKYIL 'KHOR CHA TSANG BA GCIG TU GYUR BA MDUN GYI NAM MKHAR BZHUGS PAR BSAM,
rows.wylie: rang bzhin gyi gnas 'og min ni chos sku la sogs pa rang gi nye logs kyi nam mkha' nas, nam mkha' dvangs pa las sprin blo bur du ldang ba ltar phyogs bcu'i rgyal ba thams cad dpal rdo rje 'jigs byed kyi rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rnam pa dpag tu med par spyan drangs nas ma mtha' dkyil 'khor cha tshang ba gcig tu gyur ba mdun gyi nam mkhar bzhugs par bsam
rows.english: These rays of light invite to you all the enlightened Victors of the entire universe, in limitless forms of the secret world of the shining Diamond Lord of Terror, and all the Holy Beings who reside in this world.  They come from the Land of Ultimate Reality, from the Dharma Body and the like, from the empty space around where you are.  They appear there like clouds suddenly forming in a crystal-clear sky.  At the very least you should try to visualize that one entire secret world of the Lord of Terror comes and appears in the air before you. 12 Mantras of the Beings of Pledge (Sadhana) The mantra

rows.acip: RNAM SMIN GYI LUS KYI PHUNG PO'I NANG NA GNAS PA NI SPRIN GYI GSEB NA GLOG 'GYU BA LTA BU'O, ,STONG PA'I NGANG NAS THOL GYIS BZHENGS PA NI SHIN TU DVANGS PA'I CHU LAS CHU BUR RDOL BA LTA BU'O, ,YAN LAG DANG NYING LAG THAMS CAD YONGS SU RDZOGS PA NI ME LONG LA RDO RJE 'CHANG GI GZUGS BRNYAN SHAR BA LTA BU'O,,
rows.wylie: rnam smin gyi lus kyi phung po'i nang na gnas pa ni sprin gyi gseb na glog 'gyu ba lta bu'o, ,stong pa'i ngang nas thol gyis bzhengs pa ni shin tu dvangs pa'i chu las chu bur rdol ba lta bu'o, ,yan lag dang nying lag thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa ni me long la rdo rje 'chang gi gzugs brnyan shar ba lta bu'o
rows.english: The way in which this body remains within the heap of the body which is a ripening of karma is like (10) the way that lightning flashes deep within a cloud.  So too the way that the body rises, all of a sudden, out of the state of emptiness is similar to how (11) a bubble pops up out of crystal-clear water.  The way in which we appear in this body with all our major and minor limbs complete in every way is similar to (12) the way the reflection of the Keeper of the Diamond would appear in a mirror.

rows.acip: NYAL LUGS PHYI MA LTAR NA, NAM MKHA' STONG PA LAS SPRIN RDOL BA'AM, CHU DVANGS PA LAS NYE'U CHUNG 'PHAR BA BZHIN DU BDE CHEN 'OD GSAL STONG PA NYID KYI NGANG LAS RANG NYID RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SKUR LAM GYIS LDANG STE, GNAS SOGS KYI BKOD PA'I KHYAD PAR PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR MOS,
rows.wylie: nyal lugs phyi ma ltar na, nam mkha' stong pa las sprin rdol ba'am, chu dvangs pa las nye'u chung 'phar ba bzhin du bde chen 'od gsal stong pa nyid kyi ngang las rang nyid rnal 'byor ma'i skur lam gyis ldang ste, gnas sogs kyi bkod pa'i khyad par phun sum tshogs par mos
rows.english: If you have been sleeping the second way, imagine that you waken all in a flash, as the Angel Herself, from a state of emptiness, from great bliss and the clear light.  Picture it like the way a cloud pops up all of a sudden in a clear blue sky, or the way a tiny fish suddenly leaps out of a pool of crystal water.  Try hard to imagine then that the place and other things around you are all perfectly excellent.

rows.acip: DBU MA KHYAD CHOS GSUM LDAN ZHES BYA BA DRANGS SHING 'DRONGS PA CHU SHING GI SDONG PO LTA BU, GSAL SHING DVANGS PA TIL MAR GYI MAR ME LTA BU, 'JAM ZHING MNYEN PA PADMA'I 'DAB MA LTA BU, DE'I STENG DU DMAR ZHING SNUM PA RGYA SKYEGS KYI KHU BA LTA BU BSNAN PA BZHI LDAN DU BZHED PA'ANG YOD,
rows.wylie: dbu ma khyad chos gsum ldan zhes bya ba drangs shing 'drongs pa chu shing gi sdong po lta bu, gsal shing dvangs pa til mar gyi mar me lta bu, 'jam zhing mnyen pa padma'i 'dab ma lta bu, de'i steng du dmar zhing snum pa rgya skyegs kyi khu ba lta bu bsnan pa bzhi ldan du bzhed pa'ang yod
rows.english: The central channel is said to have three qualities.  It is perfectly straight and runs erect like a rod.  It is clear and translucent like a sesame oil flame.  It is soft and pliable like the petal of a lotus flower.  On top of these some people add a fourth quality--that it is red and glistening like the sap from a {@???} plant.

rows.english: Given all this, it is easier to maintain recognition in your dreams under the following conditions. First, when your dreams are clearer in the first place. Secondly when, even if they are not normally clear, you have created a situation with all the special conditions that lend a lucid state of mind: staying in an isolated area, and the like. And finally, even with regard to a single night, those periods--such as daybreak--when your mental state is more clear.

rows.english: "What kinds of beings," one may ask, "have which of the different states of birth?" All four types of birth exist with humans. An example of instant, complete birth would be humans of the very first eon. The king called "Let- Me-Nurse-You" would typify birth from warmth and moisture. A case of humans born from eggs would be the elders Drak and Nyedrak, who were offspring of a shipwrecked merchant who coupled with a female crane. Another such instance would be that of Sagala, a woman with laywoman's vows, who gave 32 eggs from which 32 boys sprang forth. Yet another case would be that of the queen of King Panchala, who gave 500 eggs. These were put into a chest that was thrown into the Ganges River. A Lichavi youth saw the chest while washing--and when he opened the lid, 500 boys sprang forth. Examples of birth from the womb would be the majority of humans of present times.

rows.english: If you make consistent efforts in this practice, you will start to dream about washing yourself; or putting on white clothes, or new clothes; seeing pus or worms or other dirty and ugly-looking things pass out of your body; or perhaps flying unaided in the sky, or things of the like.  When you have these kinds of dreams over and over, said our Lama, it is a sign that you are truly becoming cleaned of all your wrongs. Fifth: the Practice of the Lama

rows.acip: DES NA, LAS CAN GYI 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, TSAD MTSUNGS NGES PAR DGOS PA MA YIN TE, DGOS NA, PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I NANG DU GNAS KYI BLOS GNAS SHING , THA MAL GYI MIG SHES KYIS MI BZOD PA'I SROG CHAGS PHRA MO'I MIG SHES KYIS KYANG , DE'I TSAD MAR 'GRO DGOS PA DANG , RGYA MTSO'I NANG NA GNAS PA'I SROG CHAGS PHRA MO'I MIG SHES KYIS KYANG , RGYA MTSO'I TSAD LA TSAD MAR 'GRO DGOS PA DANG , LHA MA YIN 'GA' ZHIG LA, MTSON CHA PHOR GANG SNANG DGOS PA LA SOGS PA'I SKYON YOD PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: des na, las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, tshad mtshungs nges par dgos pa ma yin te, dgos na, phor pa gang po de'i nang du gnas kyi blos gnas shing , tha mal gyi mig shes kyis mi bzod pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , de'i tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , rgya mtsho'i nang na gnas pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , rgya mtsho'i tshad la tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , lha ma yin 'ga' zhig la, mtshon cha phor gang snang dgos pa la sogs pa'i skyon yod pa'i phyir
rows.english: In conclusion now, let us consider again these three kinds of beings, each with their different karma, as they sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It's not necessarily true that they must all have valid perceptions which are identical. If they did, then the three beings looking at the glass of water would have to think of the water as a place to live, in the way that a creature living in water would. The three beings as well would have to see the water in the same way that microscopic organisms living in the water, little beings imperceptible to normal visual consciousness, see it with their own visual consciousness. Then too the visual consciousness of microscopic organisms living in the depths of the ocean would have to be a valid perception towards the entire extent of the sea. And certain kinds of near-gods too would have to see weapons as glasses of water, and on and on; the problems raised would be many.

rows.acip: DE'I BSHAD SBYAR DGE BSNYEN BTZUN PAS MDZAD PAR, CHU KLUNG GI DNGOS PO LA RANG RANG GI LAS KYI RNAM SMIN GYI DBANG GIS YI DVAGS KYIS RNAG LA SOGS PAS GANG BAR MTHONG BA DANG, DE NYID LA DUD 'GRO NYA LA SOGS PAS GNAS KYI BLOS GNAS PAR BYED PA DANG,
rows.wylie: de'i bshad sbyar dge bsnyen btsun pas mdzad par, chu klung gi dngos po la rang rang gi las kyi rnam smin gyi dbang gis yi dvags kyis rnag la sogs pas gang bar mthong ba dang, de nyid la dud 'gro nya la sogs pas gnas kyi blos gnas par byed pa dang
rows.english: The explanation of this work by the layperson with lifetime vows named “Holy One” though does give the following explanation— Each one, according to the power of their own karmic ripening, sees the stream of fresh water in a different way. The craving spirit sees it filled with pus and the like. An animal like a fish or the like sees the very same object as being their home, and they want to reside in it.

rows.acip: RANG YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS SPYI BO NAS MGRIN PAR SLEB PA NA DGA' BA, MGRIN PA NAS SNYING GAR SLEB PA NA MCHOG DGA', SNYING GNAS LTE BAR SLEB PA NA KHYAD DGA', LTE BA NAS GSANG GNAS KYI RTZER SLEB PA NA LHAN CIG SKYES BA'I DGA' BA SKYES, BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA NI DBANG GSUM BA'I NGO BO YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: rang yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i byang chub kyi sems spyi bo nas mgrin par sleb pa na dga' ba, mgrin pa nas snying gar sleb pa na mchog dga', snying gnas lte bar sleb pa na khyad dga', lte ba nas gsang gnas kyi rtser sleb pa na lhan cig skyes ba'i dga' ba skyes, bde stong dbyer med kyi lhan skyes kyi dga' ba ni dbang gsum ba'i ngo bo yin no
rows.english: (Speak then to the disciple these words, so they understand what is happening:) The two of you, The Man and Woman, Go into union. The Wish for enlightenment Flows from the top of your heads To your throats, Bringing you ecstasy. From your throats then It flows to your hearts, Bringing you high ecstasy. Flowing from your hearts To your navels, It brings you incredible ecstasy. From your navels it flows To the tips of your secret places, Bringing you simultaneous bliss. And it is this simultaneous bliss, Indivisible ecstasy and voidness, Which is the true essence Of this, the third initiation.

rows.english: The Golden Harvest explains these offerings as follows.  The outer offering consists of the offering of the five objects of enjoyment: the objects of the senses.  The secret offering is where we make offerings to the beings of a secret world which we are meditating upon, utilizing things that are subsumed within ourselves, such as our seed. The offering of suchness is where we go into union with a consort and experience the four levels of bliss, one by one, and thus actualize the state free of mental afflictions.

rows.english: How does the class of deep practice explain this point?  The masters Shakyamitra and Buddhaguhya both say that Prince Siddhartha went into deep meditation on the fourth concentration level, at the very limit, sitting on the banks of the Ranjana River.  All the Buddhas in every corner of the universe then snapped Their fingers; and the sound brought him up out of this meditation and urged him higher.

rows.wylie: des na slob dpon kun dga' snying pos, ston pa 'di bskal pa grangs med gsum du tshogs bsags nas srid pa tha mar gyur pa'i tshe, 'og min du rab mtha'i bsam gtan bzhi pa la snyoms par zhugs pa na, phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyis se gol gyi sgras bslangs pa sogs su bshad pa ltar 'dod dgos te
rows.english: As such, we would have to accept the position expressed by the master Anandagarbha.  His explanation begins by saying that our Teacher spent three countless masses of eons collecting good deeds.  Then, when he was about to reach the end of the cycle of pain, he went into deep meditation on the fourth concentration level, at the very limit, within the Heaven Below None.  At this point all the Buddhas in every corner of the universe snapped Their fingers, and the sound brought him up out of the meditation, and so on.

rows.acip: GSANG BA'I SNA RTZER RDZAS THIG BSGOM PA NI, RANG DANG LAS RGYA GNYIS SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LAS BYANG SEMS DH'U T'I'I MAR SNA GNYIS 'PHRAD MTSAMS SU 'PHO MED DU 'DZIN PA DANG , RANG DANG YE RGYA'I DH'U T'I'I MAR SNA GNYIS 'PHRAD MTSAMS SU THIG LE LA DMIGS NAS BSGOM PA GNYIS YOD DO,,
rows.wylie: gsang ba'i sna rtser rdzas thig bsgom pa ni, rang dang las rgya gnyis snyoms par zhugs pa las byang sems dhU tI'i mar sna gnyis 'phrad mtshams su 'pho med du 'dzin pa dang , rang dang ye rgya'i dhU tI'i mar sna gnyis 'phrad mtshams su thig le la dmigs nas bsgom pa gnyis yod do
rows.english: There are two ways in which we practice with a drop of substance at the opening of the secret channel.  For the first, we go into the meditation with a partner of the rite; when the element comes, then we hold it, without letting it move, at the juncture where the two lower openings of the channels of dance are touching.  For the second, we meditate, focusing on the drop at the juncture where the two channels of dance--those of ourselves and of our partner of the rite--are touching.

rows.english: The secret empowerment for these two refers, respectively, to the following.  The Lama goes into union with either one, or nine, Women of Knowledge; and then we partake of the secret substance which comes from this union. rows.english: (Continue on with:) The khatvanga staff Of your Lama, The Angel of Diamond, Transforms into the Angel Of the Union of Spheres, And We go into The meditation of union. We speak the Mantra of the Triple Om, Embellished by the three letters, Over the white and red Elements of Enlightenment. rows.acip: BAm YIG NANG GI RDO RJE BTZUN MO'I MCHOG ,CES PA'I DON PHYI'I LAS RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS NANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I BTZUN MO KHAMS DMAR PO ME'I RANG BZHIN DE SBAR BA LA BRTEN NAS SPYI BO'I KHAMS DKAR PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA DE ZHU, DE GNYIS SNYING KHAR 'DU 'PHROD BYAS PAS NA DE LTA BU'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I RTZE DGAS ROL BAR ZHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: baM yig nang gi rdo rje btsun mo'i mchog ,ces pa'i don phyi'i las rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la brten nas phyag rgya'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas nang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i btsun mo khams dmar po me'i rang bzhin de sbar ba la brten nas spyi bo'i khams dkar po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa de zhu, de gnyis snying khar 'du 'phrod byas pas na de lta bu'i rang zhal mthong ba'i rtse dgas rol bar zhog ces pa dang
rows.english: The next line of His prayer, which mentions "the inner Angel, Supreme Queen of Diamond, the sacred sound of vam," refers to the following process.  When you enjoy union with your outer partner of ritual, a wind comes from Her secret place, like a stream of smoke from a stick of incense.  This forces the downward-clearing wind within your own body to reverse direction and come up. This then causes the Queen at your navel (the red element, which is of the nature of fire) to blaze.  This blazing in turn causes the white element at the tip of your head (which is of the nature of Heruka) to melt down.  And then these two elements come together and collide at the heart.  What Master Tsarchen is praying for then is that He might laugh and play in the bliss of seeing the Angel's true face in this sense.

rows.english: Here it's best if the khatvanga staff held by every Angel in the secret world of the body transforms into Heruka; otherwise it can also be just the single staff which you hold.  This can either be Heruka with all His faces and arms, or else with just one face and two arms.  His holy body is blue; He holds a diamond and bell, and He wears the six accoutrement.  His yogi's dreadlocks are bound up in a topknot, and to the front of this knot is a crossed diamond.  To the knot's own left His head is adorned with a crescent moon.  He sports a garland around His neck made of fresh human skulls, and He goes into the meditation of union with us.

rows.wylie: bzhi pa la gsum, rig ma dang snyoms par zhugs pas bskyed pa'i bdud rtsi zos pa'i bcud len gyis lus kyi stobs rgyas par bya ba, gsung rdo rje'i lces rtsa bskul nas bde ba bskyed de las byung ba'i bdud rtsi lces myang ba dang, padma can la sogs pa'i phyag rgya rnams kyis yid dga' bar bya zhing de rnams kyi thugs sun mi dbyung pa mjug sdud dang bcas pa'o
rows.english: The fourth topic has three parts: (1) A description of how we partake of the nectar that is produced when we engage in union with our Lady of Knowledge, and how this acts as a nutritive essence which strengthens the body; (2) How we use our tongue--as the diamond of enlightened speech--to stimulate the lower end of the partner's inner channel, and produce bliss in Her; and then use our tongue again to partake of the nectar that comes from Her because of this bliss; (3) How partners such as the Lady of the Lotus are pleased, and how we must be careful never to upset their minds--along with a concluding section. * * * Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) gives some additional, useful detail on the need for both inner and outer aids in his Book to Please Those with a Core of Goodness: A Brief Explanation of the Very Essence of "The Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps," on the Stage of Completion in the Teachings of the Glorious Secret Collection (ACIP digital text S00260, ff. 26b-27a):

rows.acip: DE LA 'DIR PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS SROG RTZOL DU 'GRO BA'I TSUL, ZHES PA DA LTAR GYI GANG ZAG LA DNGOS SU MI DGOS PA SHAS CHE YANG, DE'I GO BA CHAGS NA BSKYED RIM SGOM BA SOGS KYI SKABS SU, YE RGYA LA BRTEN PA LA PHAN CHE BAS NYE BAR MKHO BA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: de la 'dir phyi rol gyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pas srog rtsol du 'gro ba'i tshul, zhes pa da ltar gyi gang zag la dngos su mi dgos pa shas che yang, de'i go ba chags na bskyed rim sgom ba sogs kyi skabs su, ye rgya la brten pa la phan che bas nye bar mkho ba yin no
rows.english: We come to a point in the text then where it talks about "how we turn union with an actual, outside partner into a practice for the control of the inner winds."  Most people nowadays aren't to the point where they would actually need this, but it is useful to gain some understanding of it.  And so at junctures such as where you are practicing the stage of creation, it can be very helpful to utilize an imaginary partner--we can even say it is a necessity. * * * The points at which we practice with the two partners are identified by Je Rinpoche in His commentary to Highest Bliss (Sanvara) entitled An Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316, folio 123b).

rows.acip: ZHAG BDUN GYIS ZHES PA NI, YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS YUN RING PO MI THOGS PAR 'THOB PA'I DON YIN GYI ZHAG BDUN LAS MI 'DA' BA'I DON MIN NO'O,,

rows.english: When the text here says "within seven days," what it means is that--if we practice union with an imaginary partner--then we will achieve our goal within no very long amount of time; it's not to say that it might not happen in a period that exceeds seven days.

rows.acip: SEMS BRTAN (YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA SEMS BRTAN PA MED PA RNAMS KYIS, PA TSAB CHAG PHYI ROL GYI ZER, KHA CIG CHAG 'GYUR GYI DE MI 'THAD DE, RGYA DPE LA DGAG SGRA GSAL BAR MED CING, 'GREL PAR SEMS BRTAN PA ZHES BSHAD PA DANG 'GAL BAS SO, ,ZHES PA DE NI MI 'THAD DE, 'GREL PAR SEMS BRTAN PA ZHES PA'I 'GYUR BTZAS PA YIN PAS GNOD BYED DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR DANG,
rows.wylie: sems brtan (ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la sems brtan pa med pa rnams kyis, pa tshab chag phyi rol gyi zer, kha cig chag 'gyur gyi de mi 'thad de, rgya dpe la dgag sgra gsal bar med cing, 'grel par sems brtan pa zhes bshad pa dang 'gal bas so, ,zhes pa de ni mi 'thad de, 'grel par sems brtan pa zhes pa'i 'gyur btsas pa yin pas gnod byed du mi rung ba'i phyir dang
rows.english: When their understanding has thus become firm, they can engage in union with an outer partner.  This will bring them, the coming lines indicate, the experience of highest bliss.  (Where the text here mentions "what is done by those who do not have a firm understanding of the practice of union with an imaginary partner," we see in the translations of Patsab and Chak "an outer partner."  Some have said that Chak's translation is incorrect, since the original Sanskrit manuscript includes no clear negative grammar particle here, and because it contradicts the commentary, which at this point says "those who do have a firm understanding."  This position though is itself incorrect, since the mention of "those of firm understanding" in the commentary is using twilight language, and is thus inappropriate to use as a line to refute some other position.)

rows.english: (We can say then that both the newer translations work out to the same thing. rows.acip: 'DI LA BSKYED RIM PAS NI SPROS PA GZHAN 'DOR MOD KYANG, CHO GA'I RIM PA NI 'DRA BAR MNGON PAS, DKYIL 'KHOR RGYAL MCHOG RDZOGS PA DANG YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS TE, DGA' BZHI'I RIM GYIS LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA BSKYED DE BDE STONG SGOM MO,,
rows.wylie: 'di la bskyed rim pas ni spros pa gzhan 'dor mod kyang, cho ga'i rim pa ni 'dra bar mngon pas, dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog rdzogs pa dang ye rgya dang snyoms par zhugs te, dga' bzhi'i rim gyis lhan skyes kyi dga' ba bskyed de bde stong sgom mo
rows.english: Now it is true that in this regard a practitioner on the stage of creation gives up other kinds of elaboration; but it would seem to me that the steps of their ritual would be similar to what we've been describing.  And so they could perform the practice of the Supreme Victor of the Secret World, and engage in union with an imaginary partner, and thus bring on the four blisses.  With this then they would in stages reach the  simultaneous form of bliss, and then could meditate on bliss and voidness.

rows.wylie: rdzogs rim gyi skabs gsum du ni sgrub thabs kyi cho ga'i rim pa ci rigs pa la brten nas ye rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa na nang gi rlung gi rnal 'byor mthar son pas grogs byas pa'i mthus, gnyis snang gi spros pa mang po bcad nas stong pa bzhi khyad par can mngon du byed do
rows.english: In the three different contexts of the practice of the stage of completion then you would take some step of the ritual that involved going into union with an imaginary partner.  You thus perfect a deep practice of working with the inner winds which then lends you support in the task of eliminating a great many forms of elaboration, in the sense of perceiving things in duality.  And then you would manifest an extraordinary form of the four forms of emptiness.

rows.acip: BAm YIG NANG GI RDO RJE BTZUN MO'I MCHOG ,CES PA'I DON PHYI'I LAS RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS NANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I BTZUN MO KHAMS DMAR PO ME'I RANG BZHIN DE SBAR BA LA BRTEN NAS SPYI BO'I KHAMS DKAR PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA DE ZHU, DE GNYIS SNYING KHAR 'DU 'PHROD BYAS PAS NA DE LTA BU'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I RTZE DGAS ROL PAR ZHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: baM yig nang gi rdo rje btsun mo'i mchog ,ces pa'i don phyi'i las rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la brten nas phyag rgya'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas nang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i btsun mo khams dmar po me'i rang bzhin de sbar ba la brten nas spyi bo'i khams dkar po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa de zhu, de gnyis snying khar 'du 'phrod byas pas na de lta bu'i rang zhal mthong ba'i rtse dgas rol par zhog ces pa dang
rows.english: The next line of His prayer, which mentions "the inner Angel, Supreme Queen of Diamond, the sacred sound of vam," refers to the following process.  When you enjoy union with your actual, outer partner, a wind comes from Her secret place, like a stream of smoke from a stick of incense.  This forces the downward-clearing wind within your own body to reverse direction and come up. This then causes the Queen at your navel (the red element, which is of the nature of fire) to blaze.  This blazing in turn causes the white element at the tip of your head (which is of the nature of Heruka) to melt down.  And then these two elements come together and collide at the heart.  What Master Tsarchen is praying for then is that He might laugh and play in the bliss of seeing the Angel's true face in this sense.

rows.acip: SNANG BA GSAL BA DANG DE BRTAN PA RNYED NA, DE DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS NAS DGA' BZHI BSKYED PA'I LHAN SKYES KYI DUS SU, BDE STONG SBYOR NUS NA LTA BA DRAN PAR BYAS LA BDE STONG DBYER MED DU BSKYANG,
rows.wylie: snang ba gsal ba dang de brtan pa rnyed na, de dang snyoms par zhugs nas dga' bzhi bskyed pa'i lhan skyes kyi dus su, bde stong sbyor nus na lta ba dran par byas la bde stong dbyer med du bskyang
rows.english: If they keep this up over a long period of time, then they will reach a point where their visualization is very clear, and firm.  They go into union with this partner, and attain the point of the simultaneous, where they are able to bring on the four forms of bliss.  If you are able thus to achieve a union of bliss and emptiness, then try to bring to mind the correct view of reality, and maintain this vision of indivisible bliss and voidness.

rows.english: "Well then," one might ask, "couldn't the stream of mind in one of the two lower realms then also rely on the discrete type of being involved, or upon life, without depending upon form?" It could not, because the mind in these cases is of little force, as it is not yet free of the conception of form. The mind of the formless realm, on the other hand, need not rely on form: because of the power of its single-pointed concentration, the mind is free of the conception of form and thus possesses considerable force.

rows.english: In response Subhuti replies, O Conqueror, it would not be so. And suppose you were to ask why—for what reason—it is so. It is because the One Gone Thus has said that other people's seeing something as a self and the rest, as described by the One Gone Thus, are ways of seeing things that would never exist anyway, at least in an ultimate sense, since the views themselves fail, and the objects which they believe they see prove to be non-existent. And this is precisely why we can call them "seeing something as a self" and the rest. Understanding & seeing

rows.english: What is the one door that a person who hopes for freedom should enter? The door is the precious instruction of the Victors—that and only that. There are many different approaches to these teachings, but only one thing decides whether someone has truly entered in. And that is whether or not this person accepts the view that things are not themselves.

rows.acip: ,SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI SEMS CAN RE RE'I 'CHI 'PHO DANG, ,SKYE GANG 'JIG RTEN LA GNAS NAM MKHA' MTHAR THUG DANG, ,BKRA MANG DE LA MKHYEN PA DUS DER 'JUG PA YIS, ,MA CHAGS RNAM KUN YONGS DAG MTHA' YAS STOBS SU 'DOD,
rows.wylie: sems can rnams kyi sems can re re'i 'chi 'pho dang, ,skye gang 'jig rten la gnas nam mkha' mthar thug dang, ,bkra mang de la mkhyen pa dus der 'jug pa yis, ,ma chags rnam kun yongs dag mtha' yas stobs su 'dod
rows.english: And then there is The death, and Moving on, that All beings Have experienced In the form of each Separate living thing; As well as the rebirth. rows.english: If with eyes made clear by this faith you begin to see your Lama as a real Buddha, then the blessing of a real Buddha will follow in your mind-stream. rows.acip: ,BDAG TU CHAGS PA'I RGYU NYID LAS, ,BDE MIN BDE BAR 'DU SHES PAS, ,KUN LA RAB TU 'JUG 'GYUR BA, ,DE PHYIR SRED PA SRID RTEN YIN,

rows.english: From the one cause of being attached to some self-nature, They conceive of what's not happiness as happiness, And as a result they dive into everything; Therefore craving's a basis for rebirth.

rows.acip: SRED PA DE DE LTAR YIN PAR THAL, BDE BA MIN PA LA BDE BAR 'DU SHES PAS NYAMS PA DAG DMAN PA'I YUL KUN LA RAB TU 'JUG PAR 'GYUR BA DE'I PHYIR, 'DU SHES PHYIN CI LOG DE RGYU MED MIN TE, DE BDAG TU CHAGS PA'I RGYU NYID LAS 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: sred pa de de ltar yin par thal, bde ba min pa la bde bar 'du shes pas nyams pa dag dman pa'i yul kun la rab tu 'jug par 'gyur ba de'i phyir, 'du shes phyin ci log de rgyu med min te, de bdag tu chags pa'i rgyu nyid las 'byung ba'i phyir
rows.english: It is true that craving is this way, because those who have been brought down by the tendency to conceive of what's not happiness as being happiness dive as a result of this into "everything," which refers to unworthy things and goals. Neither is it true that this totally mistaken backwards conception of things is without its proper cause, for all this occurs from the one cause of being attached to some self-nature.

rows.acip: GZUGS MED DANG PO GSUM LA MI BRTEN TE, DE GSUM GYIS 'DOD PA LA MI DMIGS, MTHONG LAM GYIS 'DOD PA LA DMIGS PA'I PHYIR, SRID RTZE LA MI BRTEN TE, SRID RTZE NI 'DU SHES MI GSAL PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: gzugs med dang po gsum la mi brten te, de gsum gyis 'dod pa la mi dmigs, mthong lam gyis 'dod pa la dmigs pa'i phyir, srid rtse la mi brten te, srid rtse ni 'du shes mi gsal pa'i phyir
rows.english: Neither can the ultimate stage rely upon any one of the first three formless levels, for at these levels one is incapable of focusing upon the desire level--and during the path of seeing one must. Finally, it is impossible for the ultimate stage to rely on the "peak" level--the fourth of the formless levels--for one's ability to discriminate at this level is too unclear.

rows.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, 'KHOR DANG BCAS NA PHUNG PO DU BA YIN ZHE NA, ZAG MED KYI SHES RAB KYI 'KHOR DU ZAG MED KYI SDOM PAS BSDUS PA'I RNAM PAR RIG BYED MA YIN PA'I GZUGS KYANG YOD PAS PHUNG PO LNGA PA CAN YIN LA, DE YANG BSAM GTAN DANG PO GNYIS LA BRTEN NAS YID BDE DANG GSUM PA LA BRTEN NAS SEMS BDE, BTANG SNYOMS KYI SA GZHAN GANG RUNG LA BRTEN NAS TSOR BA BTANG SNYOMS DANG , YID SHES 'KHOR DU BYUNG BA'I 'DU SHES, SEMS BYUNG 'DU BYED KYI PHUNG PO, LDAN MIN 'DU BYED CI RIGS PA YID KYI RNAM SHES DANG BCAS PA RNAMS YOD PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, 'khor dang bcas na phung po du ba yin zhe na, zag med kyi shes rab kyi 'khor du zag med kyi sdom pas bsdus pa'i rnam par rig byed ma yin pa'i gzugs kyang yod pas phung po lnga pa can yin la, de yang bsam gtan dang po gnyis la brten nas yid bde dang gsum pa la brten nas sems bde, btang snyoms kyi sa gzhan gang rung la brten nas tshor ba btang snyoms dang , yid shes 'khor du byung ba'i 'du shes, sems byung 'du byed kyi phung po, ldan min 'du byed ci rigs pa yid kyi rnam shes dang bcas pa rnams yod pa'i phyir
rows.english: How many heaps does knowledge have, if you count all of those which are attendant to it? Knowledge can be said to have all five heaps, since unstained wisdom comes along with non-communicating form included within unstained restraint. Feeling is present as pleasure of thought if the wisdom relies on the first two concentration levels. Where it relies on the third, mental pleasure is had. Reliance on other levels, of neutral feeling, means that neutral feeling is present. Discrimination is there as an attendant to consciousness of one's thoughts, as well as the heap of other factors--be they mental functions or the factors not associated with mind--along with consciousness.

rows.english: Here is the first. One may ask, "How do you define the act of killing?" The Abbreviation says that five parts are involved: the object, the conception, the thinking, the bad thought, and the conclusion. These five can be shortened into four: the middle three can be included into the thinking, and we can add the stage of undertaking; this makes the presentation easier, and in no way violates the intention of the original text.

rows.english: The part of the thinking has three components of its own. Conception can be of four different types: to conceive of the object, say a living being, as being a living being; to conceive of a living being as something other than a living being; to conceive of something other than a living being as being other than a living being, and to conceive of this same thing as a living being. The first and third types of conception here are unmistaken; the second and fourth are mistaken.

Conception can be of four different types: to conceive of the object, say a living being, as being a living being; to conceive of a living being as something other than a living being; to conceive of something other than a living being as being other than a living being, and to conceive of this same thing as a living being. rows.english: This is a particular feature of the motivation. Suppose, for example, that you think to yourself, "I only want to kill John," and undertake the deed. Then you mistake Joe for John, and kill Joe. In this sort of case, there is no "actual- commission" stage; so we can see that, for this stage, the conception you have must be unmistaken. If on the other hand you undertake the deed with some general kind of motivation, if you think to yourself, "I'll kill anyone I happen to meet," then this detail of the conception having to be unmistaken need not be complete. You should understand that this point applies to the other nine as well.

rows.english: There was a time before when, for three months, the Teacher pretended to be so destitute that he was forced to eat the barley that we usually use for horse fodder. His disciple Ananda was depressed by the sight, thinking to himself, "Now the day has come that the Teacher, who was born into royalty, is reduced to eating horse fodder." The Teacher then took a single piece of the grain from his mouth, handed it to Ananda, and instructed him to eat it. The disciple complied, and was filled; in fact, for an entire week thereafter he felt no urge to eat anything at all, and was overcome with amazement. This incident applies here too.

rows.wylie: rab 'byor, 'di la byang chub sems dpa'i theg pa la yang dag par zhugs pas 'di snyam du, bdag gis ji tsam sems can du bsdu bas bsdus pa sgo nga las skyes pa'am, mngal nas skyes pa'am, drod gsher las skyes pa'am, brdzus te skyes pa'am, gzugs can nam, gzugs med pa'am, 'du shes can nam, 'du shes med pa'am, 'du shes med 'du shes med min nam, sems can gyi khams ji tsam sems can du gdags pas btags pa de dag thams cad phung po lhag ma med pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa'i dbyings su yongs su mya ngan las bzla'o, , de ltar sems can tshad med pa yongs su mya ngan las bzlas kyang sems can gang yang yongs su mya ngan las bzlas par gyur pa med do, , snyam du sems bskyed par bya'o
rows.english: Subhuti, this is how those who have entered well into the way of the bodhisattva must think to themselves as they feel the Wish to achieve enlightenment: I will bring to nirvana the total amount of living beings, every single one numbered among the ranks of living kind: those who were born from eggs, those who were born from a womb, those who were born through warmth and moisture, those who were born miraculously, those who have a physical form, those with none, those with conceptions, those with none, and those with neither conceptions nor no conceptions. However many living beings there are, in whatever realms there may be--anyone at all labelled with the name of "living being"--all these will I bring to total nirvana, to the sphere beyond all grief, where none of the parts of the person are left at all. Yet even if I do manage to bring this limitless number of living beings to total nirvana, there will be no living being at all who was brought to total nirvana.

rows.english: What the root text is saying is: "Subhuti, this is how those who have entered the way of the bodhisattva must think to themselves first as they feel the Wish to achieve enlightenment: Whatever realms there may be, and however many living beings there are, they reach to infinity, they are countless. If one were to classify those numbered among the ranks of living kind by type of birth, there would be four: those who were born from eggs, and then those who were born from a womb, those who were born through warmth and moisture, and those who were born miraculously. Then again there are the sentient beings living in the desire realm and the form realm: those who have a physical form. There are also the beings in the formless realm: those with no physical form. There are "those with conceptions," meaning the beings who live in all the levels except the ones known as the "great result" and the "peak of existence." There are "those with no conceptions," which refers to a portion of the beings who reside at the level of the great result. In addition are the beings who have been born at the level of the peak of existence: those with no coarse kinds of conceptions but who on the other hand are not such that they have no subtle conceptions. The point, in short, is that I speak of all living beings: of anyone at all labelled with the name of "living being." All these will I bring to total nirvana, to the sphere beyond all grief, where one no longer remains in either of the extremes--and

rows.english: The King of Concentration says as well, You should apply what you understand about how You think of your "self" to every thing there is. All this is true as well for objects like the perfection of giving and so on: they exist only through being labelled with a term, and are empty of any natural existence. Seeking to make us realize how necessary it is to understand this fact, Lord Buddha makes statements like "Perform the act of giving without believing in any object at all."

rows.english: This is the most important thing for us to learn: so long as we are still not free of the chains of grasping to things as truly existing, and so long as we have yet to grasp the meaning of emptiness, then we will never be able to achieve freedom, even if the Buddha should appear himself and try to lead us there. This is supported by the words of the savior Nagarjuna: Freedom is a complete impossibility For anyone who does not understand emptiness. Those who are blind will continue to circle Here in the prison of six different births. Master Aryadeva as well has spoken that "For those who conceive of things, freedom does not exist." And there are many other such quotations.

rows.english: O Conqueror, what will happen in the future, in the days of the last five hundred, when the holy Dharma is approaching its final destruction? How could anyone of those times ever see accurately the meaning of the explanations given in sutras such as this one? And the Conqueror bespoke, O Subhuti, you should never ask the question you have just asked: "What will happen in the future, in the days of the last five hundred, when the Dharma is approaching its final destruction? How could anyone of those times ever see accurately the meaning of the explanations given in sutras such as this one?"

rows.english: One may ask the reason why the above is so. It's because these particular bodhisattvas will entertain no manifest conception of something as a self, or as a living being, or as being alive, or as a person. The denotation of the words "self" and "person" and so on here are the same as I have mentioned earlier. Master Kamalashila at this point says: The expression "conceive of something as a self" means thinking "me," or grasping that the self exists. "Conceiving of something as a living being" means grasping that something belonging to the self exists. "Conceiving of something as being alive" means continuing to grasp to the same "self" as above, but for the entire length of its life. "Conceiving of something as a person" means grasping that those who are born again and again are born. Thus the meaning of grasping to something as belonging to the self is a bit different than before. When the text says that these bodhisattvas entertain no such coarse conceptions, it is referring specifically to the occasions at which one realizes the lack of a self-nature.

rows.english: O Subhuti, these bodhisattvas who are great beings neither entertain any conception of things as things, nor do they entertain any conception of things as not being things. They neither entertain any conception of a thought as a conception, nor do they entertain any conception of a thought as not being conception. Why is it so? Because if, o Subhuti, these bodhisattvas who are great beings were to entertain any conception of things as things, then they would grasp these same things as being a "self"; they would grasp them as being a living being; they would grasp them as being something that lives; they would grasp them as a person. And even if they were to entertain them as not being things, that too they would grasp as being a "self"; they would grasp as being a living being; they would grasp as being something that lives; they would grasp as a person.

rows.english: The text is saying: "Not only do these beings avoid entertaining a belief in things as being something true; neither do they entertain any conception of physical form and other things as being true things nominally. Nor as well do they entertain any conception where they believe that these things are not things." From another point of view, it is appropriate as well to gloss the passage as follows. Physical form and other such things are deceptive objects, and deceptive objects are not something which is true. These bodhisattvas avoid entertaining even the conception where one believes that this fact itself is something true. If one in fact did entertain such a conception, then certain problems would arise--and this explains the relevance of the two paragraphs that come next in the root text, the one that mentions "If they were to entertain any conception of things as things" and so on; and the other that starts with "If they were to entertain them as not being things" that had a self. 47 The Asian Classics Institute Course VI: The Diamond-Cutter Sutra Reading Five: Emptiness and Karma The following selections are taken from Sunlight on the Path to Freedom, written by Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) of Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery. The original root text of the sutra by Lord Buddha is included in darker type.

rows.acip: RGYU MTSAN NI RAB 'BYOR SNGON GYI DUS GANG GI TSE KA LING KA'I RGYAL POS NGA KHO RANG GI BUD MED DANG 'BREL LAM SNYAM PA'I DOGS NGAN BYUNG STE RAL GRIS NGA'I YAN LAG DANG NYING LAG SOR MO RNAMS BCAD PAR GYUR PA DE'I TSE, NGAS BZOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM BDEN MED DU SHES NAS BZOD PA BSGOMS PAS, THA SNYAD PA'I NGA LA DMIGS NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU BDAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES NAS GANG ZAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES KYANG MA BYUNG ZHING , DE'I TSE NGA LA DE LTA BU'I BDEN ZHEN GYI 'DU SHES CI YANG MED LA, THA SNYAD DU 'DU SHES GZHAN MED PAR GYUR PA YANG MA YIN TE, BZOD DO SNYAM PA'I SDUG BSNGAL DANG LEN DANG GNOD PA LA JI MI SNYAM PA DANG , BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I CHOS LA NGES SEMS KYI 'DU SHES RNAMS YOD PA'I PHYIR RO SNYAM DU DGONGS SO,
rows.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni rab 'byor sngon gyi dus gang gi tshe ka ling ka'i rgyal pos nga kho rang gi bud med dang 'brel lam snyam pa'i dogs ngan byung ste ral gris nga'i yan lag dang nying lag sor mo rnams bcad par gyur pa de'i tshe, ngas bzod pa'i 'khor gsum bden med du shes nas bzod pa bsgoms pas, tha snyad pa'i nga la dmigs nas nga'o snyam du bdag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes nas gang zag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes kyang ma byung zhing , de'i tshe nga la de lta bu'i bden zhen gyi 'du shes ci yang med la, tha snyad du 'du shes gzhan med par gyur pa yang ma yin te, bzod do snyam pa'i sdug bsngal dang len dang gnod pa la ji mi snyam pa dang , bden med du rtogs pa'i chos la nges sems kyi 'du shes rnams yod pa'i phyir ro snyam du dgongs so
rows.english: For what reason is it so? Because long ago there was a time, o Subhuti, when the king of Kalingka got the evil suspicion that I had engaged in relations with his woman. And so he was cutting off the larger limbs, and smaller appendages of my body. (The latter refers to the fingers and toes.) At that moment I practiced patience, keeping my mind on an understanding of the lack of true existence to each of the three elements to the act of patience. As I focussed on the "me" which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing "me": and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing "self" up to a truly existing "person." At that moment I had no conception at all of any such conception that something was existing truly. At the same time though it was neither as if I had no other, nominal conceptions at all. What Subhuti is saying here is the following. I did have the thought that I would have to keep my patience: I did have the thought to take the pain on willingly, and not to be upset about the harm being done to me. And I did have the kind of conception where I reconfirmed my knowledge of how I had perceived that no existing object has any true existence.

rows.wylie: de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor, gal te de'i tshe bdag tu 'du shes byung na, de'i tshe gnod sems kyi 'du shes kyang 'byung la, sems can du 'du shes pa dang , srog tu 'du shes pa dang , gang zag tu 'du shes pa byung na, de'i tshe gnod sems kyi 'du shes kyang 'byung ba'i phyir ro
rows.english: Why is it so? Suppose, o Subhuti, that at that moment any conception of a self had come into my mind. Then the thought to harm someone would have come into my mind as well. The conception of some sentient being, and the conception of some living being, and the conception of person, would have come into my mind. And because of that, the thought to harm someone would have come into my mind as well.
