rows.acip: MDOR BSDU NA BLA MA GCIG LAS DBANG BSKUR THOB PA'I RDO RJE SPUN YIN PA, SNGAGS KYI SDOM PA DANG LDAN PA, DER 'DU SHES NA, ZHE SDANG GIS KUN NAS BSLANGS NAS DE'I SKYON BRJOD PA, BRJOD PA DE THOS NAS DON GO BA STE CHOS LNGA TSANG BA NI RTZA LTUNG GSUM PA YIN NO,
rows.wylie: mdor bsdu na bla ma gcig las dbang bskur thob pa'i rdo rje spun yin pa, sngags kyi sdom pa dang ldan pa, der 'du shes na, zhe sdang gis kun nas bslangs nas de'i skyon brjod pa, brjod pa de thos nas don go ba ste chos lnga tshang ba ni rtsa ltung gsum pa yin no
rows.english: To summarize, a person commits the third of the root downfalls if five different elements are all complete: (1) they and the other person are diamond sisters or brothers, in that they have received empowerment from the same Lama; (2) they possess the vows of the secret word; (3) they realize that the other person is one of their diamond sisters or brothers; (4) they say something bad about the other person, out of a motivation of anger; and (5) the other person hears what they have said, and understand its meaning. *** Returning to Geshe Tsewang Samdrup for the next root downfall:

rows.acip: DBANG MTSAN NYID DANG LDAN PAS SNOD RUNG DU MA BYAS PA'I GANG ZAG LA DER 'DU SHES PA'I LHA'I RNAL 'BYOR LA SOGS PA'I SNGAGS KYI GSANG BA GANG YANG RUNG BA BSGRAGS PA PHA ROL POS DON GO NA, MA SMIN PA LA GSANG BA BSGRAGS PA'I RTZA LTUNG ,
rows.wylie: dbang mtshan nyid dang ldan pas snod rung du ma byas pa'i gang zag la der 'du shes pa'i lha'i rnal 'byor la sogs pa'i sngags kyi gsang ba gang yang rung ba bsgrags pa pha rol pos don go na, ma smin pa la gsang ba bsgrags pa'i rtsa ltung
rows.english: Suppose there is someone who has not yet been made a proper vessel for a certain teaching by receiving an authentic empowerment into that teaching -- and that we understand them to be so.  And suppose that we then share with them any of the hidden teachings of the Secret Way: teachings such as the deep practice of the Angel.  At the moment when this other person grasps what we are saying, then we have committed the root downfall known as [7] "Sharing secrets with those who are not yet ripe for them." *** Je Tsongkapa comments:

rows.acip: LAKshAMI KA RAS PHA ROL POS DON GO BA DANG DER 'DU SHES PA DANG DGOS PA KHYAD PAR CAN MED PA YANG DGOS PAR BSHAD DO,
rows.wylie: lakShami ka ras pha rol pos don go ba dang der 'du shes pa dang dgos pa khyad par can med pa yang dgos par bshad do
rows.english: Lakshmikara states that, for us to break the vow, the following conditions must as well be present: the other person understands the meaning of what we are saying; we perceive of the situation correctly; and there is no compelling need for revealing the secret. ***

rows.acip: DE LTAR NA DBANG BSKUR NAS SMIN PAR MA BYAS PA GSANG BA BSGRAGS PA LA MA DAD PA SKYE BA, DE LA DER 'DU SHES PA, THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I GSANG BA BSGRAGS PA, DE GO BA GZHAN 'DUL BA'I DGOS PA CHEN PO DANG MI LDAN PA'I CHOS DRUG TSANG NA RTZA LTUNG BDUN PA YIN NO,
rows.wylie: de ltar na dbang bskur nas smin par ma byas pa gsang ba bsgrags pa la ma dad pa skye ba, de la der 'du shes pa, thun mong ma yin pa'i gsang ba bsgrags pa, de go ba gzhan 'dul ba'i dgos pa chen po dang mi ldan pa'i chos drug tshang na rtsa ltung bdun pa yin no
rows.english: As such, we can say that six different conditions must all be present in order for someone to commit the seventh of the root downfalls.  (1) We must reveal secrets to a person whose heart has not yet been ripened through the process of empowerment, and (2) they must lose their faith.  (3) We must conceive of the situation properly, and (4) we must be revealing some secret which is not already shared.  (5) They must understand what we are saying to them, and  (6) there must not be any other, extraordinary purpose served by doing so: some way in which revealing the secret helps further their spiritual practice, taming them somehow. *** Geshe Tsewang Samdrup on the eighth of the root downfalls:

rows.wylie: rang bde mchog dang rig ma phag mor bskyed pa lus lha'i 'du shes dang , gnyis ka'i mkha' gsang byin gyis brlabs nas yi ge bkod pa sngags kyi 'du shes dang , thabs 'di la brten nas zag med kyi bde ba mngon du bya'o snyam pa'i chos kyi 'du shes te 'du shes gsum dang ldan pas snyoms 'jug bya
rows.english: The practice of union must be performed with three different conceptions.  First, we must conceive of ourselves as the Angel named Highest Bliss, and our Woman of Knowledge as the Sow.  This is called "the conception of our body as the Angel." Secondly, we must bless the sky and the secret, placing the secret syllables.  This is called the "conception of the mantra."  Finally, we must have the "conception of the Dharma," which means that we think to ourselves, "By using this method, I will be able to bring about the bliss of the immaculate." *** Returning to Geshe Tsewang Samdrup:

rows.english: The folllowing line [in the Tibetan] advises us to "Partake of the opening without dislike."  This is a reference to times when we are "partaking of the opening" in the sense of using our tongue to take the element of enlightenment out of our consort's lotus.  We must drink of this essence, we must partake of it,  "without dislike"--meaning without any kind of idea that it is something dirty.  This is the eighth of the pledges. ************

rows.acip: NYAN BSHAD KYI SKOR GZHAN BYANG CHUB LAM RIM LAS BYUNG BA LTAR DANG, SNOD KYI SKYON GSUM SPANG ZHING, 'DU SHES DRUG BSTEN PA'I STENG, GNAS KHANG DANG CHOS GROGS LA DAG PA'I SNANG BA BSGOM PA, CHOS STON PA'I BLA MA LA RGYUD KYI STON PA RDO RJE 'CHANG DU MOS PA BCAS DGOS,
rows.wylie: nyan bshad kyi skor gzhan byang chub lam rim las byung ba ltar dang, snod kyi skyon gsum spang zhing, 'du shes drug bsten pa'i steng, gnas khang dang chos grogs la dag pa'i snang ba bsgom pa, chos ston pa'i bla ma la rgyud kyi ston pa rdo rje 'chang du mos pa bcas dgos
rows.english: When our Lama had finished with all the above, which is only a short description of the greatness of this path, He spoke some on the subject of how to give and how to listen to a teaching, as it is presented in the texts on the steps of the path to Buddhahood.  We were to avoid the three "problems of the pot," and to use the six conceptions.  On top of this, we were to practice seeing the place around us, and our fellow Dharma students, as being totally pure.  And we were to think of the Lama giving the teaching as the Teacher of the Secrets, as the Holder of the Diamond Himself.

rows.acip: DE YANG LUS LA BDE DROD CHE BA DANG GNYID 'THUG PAR 'DOD NA NYI DKYIL DROD CHIL LE BA DANG, DRAN SHES GSAL ZHING GNYID BSRAB PAR 'DOD NA GNAS DANG NYI DKYIL 'OD 'TSER BZHIN PA BSAM, 'DI LAM RIM DU SNANG BA'I 'DU SHES BSKYED PAR GSUNGS PA DANG DON 'DRA,
rows.wylie: de yang lus la bde drod che ba dang gnyid 'thug par 'dod na nyi dkyil drod chil le ba dang, dran shes gsal zhing gnyid bsrab par 'dod na gnas dang nyi dkyil 'od 'tsher bzhin pa bsam, 'di lam rim du snang ba'i 'du shes bskyed par gsungs pa dang don 'dra
rows.english: If you want to have a pleasant, more warm sensation in your body, and a deeper sleep, then picture the sundisk as toasty, radiating warmth.  If you would rather have clearer thoughts and a lighter sleep, then picture the sundisk as shining brightly.  The point of this exercise is similar to that of utilizing the conception of light, which is taught in the texts on the steps of the path to Buddhahood.

rows.wylie: sa lugs la bla rnal thun mong ba ma gtogs thun mong min pa snyan brgyud kho nar mdzad pas dngul chu'i sgrub thabs su thun mong ba mdzad, de'ang bla ma dpa' bo rdo rje chos su bskyed pa thun mong ba, sangs rgyas rdo rje chos su bskyed pa thun mong ma yin pa yin, de gnyis ngo bo gcig cing, bla ma la sangs rgyas dngos kyi 'du shes yod na rnam pa sangs rgyas su bsgom ma bsgoms la khyad med kyang
rows.english: According to the Sakya tradition the unique practice of the Lama, as opposed to the shared one, can only be passed down orally, and so in Ngulchu's ritual for reaching the Angel he has used the shared one.  Now producing your Lama as Dharma of Diamond the Warrior is the shared practice, and producing Her or Him as Dharma of Diamond the Buddha is the unique practice.  In fact these two beings have one and the same nature; and if you see your Lama as the Buddha himself, it makes no difference whether you meditate on Him in the form of the Buddha or not.

rows.acip: YANG, KU SU LU NI 'DU SHES GSUM PA'AM, MA BCOS LHUG PA'I DON TE, SPROS MED DANG BCOS MED KYI NGANG NAS NANG GI NYAMS LEN BZANG BA ZHIG LA BYED PAS, 'DI'ANG NANG GI YON TAN LA MA BLTOS BAR PHYI'I SPYOD LAM LA BLTOS NAS BTAGS PA YIN PAS SNGA MA DANG 'DI GNYIS KA'I 'BAB SO GCIG TU 'ONG,
rows.wylie: yang, ku su lu ni 'du shes gsum pa'am, ma bcos lhug pa'i don te, spros med dang bcos med kyi ngang nas nang gi nyams len bzang ba zhig la byed pas, 'di'ang nang gi yon tan la ma bltos bar phyi'i spyod lam la bltos nas btags pa yin pas snga ma dang 'di gnyis ka'i 'bab so gcig tu 'ong
rows.english: There is also a word kusulu, which can refer to one of those "three thought" people, who think only of eating, sleeping, and going to the bathroom.  This same term can mean unartificial, or natural.  It describes a person who is keeping up a pure practice within themself, without any artifice, without any pretense.  The word is applied then on the basis of the person's outer behavior, without regard to their inner qualities.  Thus the two words, kusali and kusulu, really amount to the same thing.

rows.acip: RANG LUS TSOGS SU 'BUL BA LA, RNYING MA RNAMS KU SU LU ZHES PA'I DON MA BCOS LHUG PA DANG, SA CHEN SOGS GSAR MA RNAMS KU S'A LI ZHES PA DGE BA CAN LA 'JUG PAS DAG PA YIN ZHES TSUL GNYIS LAS DON DGE RTZA BSKRUN PA LA ZER BA'I DON 'DRA BAS 'DU SHES GSUM PA ZHES BYA STE, DE LA YANG ZA BA DANG NYAL BA DANG BSHANG GCI 'DOR BA STE DE GSUM LAS GZHAN GANG YANG MI BYED PA BYED LUGS NGAN PA'I TSAD LA YANG ZER ZHING,
rows.wylie: rang lus tshogs su 'bul ba la, rnying ma rnams ku su lu zhes pa'i don ma bcos lhug pa dang, sa chen sogs gsar ma rnams ku sA li zhes pa dge ba can la 'jug pas dag pa yin zhes tshul gnyis las don dge rtsa bskrun pa la zer ba'i don 'dra bas 'du shes gsum pa zhes bya ste, de la yang za ba dang nyal ba dang bshang gci 'dor ba ste de gsum las gzhan gang yang mi byed pa byed lugs ngan pa'i tshad la yang zer zhing
rows.english: Next, is the practice of offering your body as the offering of the tantric feast.  The Ancient Ones call this practice kusulu, which means "natural and uncontrived." The newer traditions--represented by sages such as the great Sakya patriarch Sachen Kunga Nyingpo--say that the word is more correctly rendered as kusali, since this means "one who possesses virtue."  However, the meaning of both of these is similar in that they refer to someone who has given rise to the inner core of virtue. The words then are also applied to "the one with three thoughts."  The mark of a really lousy character is not to do anything other eating, sleeping and going to the bathroom; and this is what we call such a person.

rows.english: At this point, said our Lama, you must turn back into the Holy Lady.  He described then how We must sit together in the meditation of union, maintaining the three different conceptions.  With steady thoughts of supreme confidence and clear vision we conceive of our bodies as Angels.  We conceive of our speech as secret words, due to the blessing of the sky within our secret Angel.  We think to ourselves,  "I shall use this practice as a means to reach immaculate bliss," and conceive of this state of mind as the Dharma. *  *  *  *  * The following selection is from The Secret Treasure of the Angels (ACIP digital text S0202), written by Lama Quicksilver, Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra (1772-1851), folios 86A-90A.

rows.acip: STONG NYID LAS LDANG NAS KYANG THUN MTSAMS KYI SKABS GZHAN DANG, LHAG PAR DGONG MO GNYID LOG PA'I SKABS LTA BUR 'DU SHES RAGS PA RNAMS BSDUS ZIN PA'I DBANG GIS GDON BGEGS KYI BAR CHAD 'JUG SLA BAS NYAL KHA SOGS SU GO CHA DANG TSAMS RNGAMS KYI SRUNG BA NAN TAN DANG, THUN MONG BA'I SRUNG 'KHOR BSGOM PA GAL CHE,
rows.wylie: stong nyid las ldang nas kyang thun mtshams kyi skabs gzhan dang, lhag par dgong mo gnyid log pa'i skabs lta bur 'du shes rags pa rnams bsdus zin pa'i dbang gis gdon bgegs kyi bar chad 'jug sla bas nyal kha sogs su go cha dang tshams rngams kyi srung ba nan tan dang, thun mong ba'i srung 'khor bsgom pa gal che
rows.english: It is not only as you rise out of the state of emptiness that you should do the practices of protection.  You need to do so as well at every other occasion spent between meditation periods.  Most especially you will have to rely on these practices in times like at night, when you sleep.  This is because your rough states of conceptual thought withdraw during these periods, a condition which makes it easy for harmful and obstructing spirits to make their entrance and create obstacles for you.  Therefore it is extremely important that--as you fall off to sleep and at other such times--you make a special effort to protect yourself with the armor and the Words of Wrath, and meditate as well on the circles of protection which are shared throughout the practice.

rows.english: That saying "Mr. Three Thoughts" refers to eating & drinking, sleeping, and relieving one's bowels.  It is like the measure of a sloth--anyone who does nothing other than those three things.  And here too, the way it appears on the outside, the person is not acting like a great scholar or meditator, and they are not engaging in the practices of recitation, prostrations, or making offerings; instead, day and night around the clock they are just lazing around.

rows.english: The word "mind" refers to the heap of different kinds of consciousness, and to the door of sense of the thought.  The expression "function of the mind" is a reference to the three heaps of feelings, discriminations, and other factors--and by extension to the object taken by the thought; that is, the door of sense called "objects."  Again, the point is that none of these has any nature of its own.

rows.english: Now it is admittedly true that the Sutra Requested by the Householder Named Ugra does say that a person who is unable to leave behind the sexual activity of a family person can follow the code of life of a bodhisattva who engages in the family life.  But then we also see the mention that "Those who have no attraction to travelling the path using the way of desire tend to think of using desire for spiritual means as a problem."  As such, the type of case we've just mentioned is not the same thing as where someone attracted to desire is guided by the path of the unsurpassed teachings.

rows.english: Here then is the second.  When we are engaged in union with our partner, we must maintain a conception of our form as that of a divine Being, utilizing a firm identification of ourselves with Her, and a clear picture of ourselves as Her as well.  But suppose that we don't have this conception, and that further we fail perform the proper blessings of ourselves and our Woman of Knowledge prior to the practice, with rituals such as the Secret Sky.  That is, suppose that we fail to maintain a conception of our own words as being mantra.

rows.english: Suppose as well that we fail to have a conception of our own mind as being the Dharma itself--where we hope to dispel other's lack of faith, and where we maintain a motivation that, through engaging in these particular means, we will be able to bring on immaculate bliss.  Or suppose further that we engage in practice with a Woman of Knowledge in any other way which is prohibited in the secret teachings--practicing with Her, for example, at the wrong time.  We will then incur this serious offense. * * * An important set of tantric vows common to most tantric systems consists of those of the Five Enlightened Families.  As we see from Geshe Tsewang Samdrup (S00201, f. 27a), one of these stipulates that we practice with a spiritual partner.

rows.english: Master Langka has the line as "Never feel dislike when you take the element of enlightenment," whereas Master Kelnden explains it as "Never be angered, and never give it up."  The point here is as Master Shura explains it: When we take the element of enlightenment, we must never do so with any feeling that this is something dirty.  This is the way it should be taken, because when we consider something impure or disgusting, this is a kind of dislike that can turn us away from the particular object.  We also see the wording elsewhere as "Disliking this type of thing."

rows.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

rows.english: The one-day vows are called "staying close" because they help you stay close to nirvana in the sense of taking you there. The lifetime vows for laymen and laywomen are called "close to virtue" because they help you be close to virtue, which here refers to nirvana. The vows of male novices and female novices are called "way to virtue" because those who possess these vows have entered the way, that is the path, which leads to virtue, again referring to nirvana. The vows of an intermediate nun are called "versed in virtue" because these women are versing themselves in the twelve rules, in order to be able to keep the vows of a fully ordained nun. Fully ordained monks and fully ordained nuns are called "begging for virtue" because they are begging, that is seeking, that state of virtue: nirvana. In this verse Je Tsongkapa is thus listing the eight kinds of individual freedom vows. 31 The Asian Classics Institute Course IX: The Ethical Life Reading Four: A General Description of the Vows, Part One The following selection consists of the second major section of Daymaker (Nyin- byed), composed by Master Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra (1772-1851) as a commentary to the Essence of the Ocean of Discipline ('Dul-ba rgya-mtso'i snying- po), a summary of the vinaya teachings by Je Tsongkapa (1357-1419). ************

rows.acip: [III.157-8a] REG PA'I ZAS LA SOGS PA DE DAG GI NGO BO GANG ZHE NA, REG PA DANG SEMS PA DANG RNAM PAR SHES PA NI ZAG PA DANG BCAS PA ZAS YIN GYI, ZAG MED ZAS MIN TE, ZAS KYI DON NI SRID PA GSO BAR BYED PA YIN NA, ZAG MED NI SRID PA ZAD BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG , MDO LAS, SEMS CAN BYUNG BA RNAMS GNAS PAR BYED PA DANG , 'TSO BAR BYED PA DANG , SRID PA TSOL BA RNAMS LA PHAN 'DOGS PAR BYED PA'O, , ZHES DANG ,
rows.wylie: [iii.157-8a] reg pa'i zas la sogs pa de dag gi ngo bo gang zhe na, reg pa dang sems pa dang rnam par shes pa ni zag pa dang bcas pa zas yin gyi, zag med zas min te, zas kyi don ni srid pa gso bar byed pa yin na, zag med ni srid pa zad byed yin pa'i phyir dang , mdo las, sems can byung ba rnams gnas par byed pa dang , 'tsho bar byed pa dang , srid pa tshol ba rnams la phan 'dogs par byed pa'o, , zhes dang
rows.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

rows.english: The explanation of this work by the layperson with lifetime vows named “Holy One” though does give the following explanation— Each one, according to the power of their own karmic ripening, sees the stream of fresh water in a different way. The craving spirit sees it filled with pus and the like. An animal like a fish or the like sees the very same object as being their home, and they want to reside in it.

rows.acip: ,DE NAS RAB 'BYOR GYIS BDAG THA SNYAD DU NYON MONGS SPANGS PA'I DGRA BCOM PA LAGS KYANG , BDAG GIS BDAG NI DGRA BCOM PA'O SNYAM DU BDEN PAR MI 'DZIN LAGS SO ZHES DANG , GAL TE DE LTAR 'DZIN NA NI BDAG KYANG NYON MONGS CAN DU 'GYUR BAS DGRA BCOM PA MA YIN PAR 'GYUR RO, , BDAG NI DGRA BCOM PA YIN TE, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS BDAG LA THA SNYAD DU RIGS KYI BU RAB 'BYOR NI NYON MONGS PA MED PA RNAMS KYI MCHOG TU LUNG BSTAN LA, DON DAM PAR CI LA YANG MI GNAS PAS NA NYON MONGS PA MED PAR GNAS PAR ZHES LUNG MI STON TE, DON DAM PAR GNAS BYA DANG GNAS BYED DANG GNAS PA PO GANG YANG MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES BSHAD DE, THAL 'GYUR BAS BDEN 'DZIN NYON MONGS SU BZHED PA DANG MTHUN NO,
rows.wylie: de nas rab 'byor gyis bdag tha snyad du nyon mongs spangs pa'i dgra bcom pa lags kyang , bdag gis bdag ni dgra bcom pa'o snyam du bden par mi 'dzin lags so zhes dang , gal te de ltar 'dzin na ni bdag kyang nyon mongs can du 'gyur bas dgra bcom pa ma yin par 'gyur ro, , bdag ni dgra bcom pa yin te, bcom ldan 'das kyis bdag la tha snyad du rigs kyi bu rab 'byor ni nyon mongs pa med pa rnams kyi mchog tu lung bstan la, don dam par ci la yang mi gnas pas na nyon mongs pa med par gnas par zhes lung mi ston te, don dam par gnas bya dang gnas byed dang gnas pa po gang yang ma grub pa'i phyir ro zhes bshad de, thal 'gyur bas bden 'dzin nyon mongs su bzhed pa dang mthun no
rows.english: Then Subhuti explains, "I am, nominally speaking, a foe destroyer. But it is also true that I do not, while grasping to some true existence, think to myself, "I am a foe destroyer." If I did grasp to it this way then I would start to have mental afflictions, and then I would stop being a foe destroyer. I am a foe destroyer, and the Conqueror has given me the final prediction: he has told me, "Nominally speaking Subhuti, son of noble family, you will reach the highest of all those states that are free of the mental afflictions." In an ultimate sense though, because I stay in no state at all, he could never have given me the final prediction, he could never have said, "O son of noble family, o Subhuti, you will reach the state free of mental afflictions." This is because, ultimately speaking, there does not even exist any place to stay, no thing to make one stay there, nor even anyone who stays there. All this is consistent with the position of the Consequence school, which says that grasping to some true existence is a mental affliction.

rows.wylie: gson rkyen rnams kyang 'chi rkyen du ma gyur pa med de, mi 'chi ba'i phyir du ni bza' btung dang gnas khang dang grogs la sogs pa rnams tshol la, de dag kyang bza' btung ha cang mangs pa dang ha cang nyungs pa dang mi 'phrod pa longs spyad pa sogs dang , gnas khang rdib pa dang mdza' bos bslus pa la sogs pa'i sgo nas 'chi ba'i rkyen du 'gyur bas na 'chi ba'i rkyen du ma song ba'i gson pa'i rkyen mi snang ngo
rows.english: Beyond all this is the fact that there is nothing at all that we use to keep ourselves alive that cannot also turn into something that kills us. We spend our lives searching for food and drink, or a place to stay, or friends or the like, with the intent that they help keep us from dying. But they can all turn into something that kills us instead. If we eat or drink too much, or too little, or ingest something which is not clean or the like, it can kill us. Our house can collapse on us, and our friends can cheat us, and they can all in the end lead us to our deaths. You literally cannot find anything that is supposed to keep you alive that cannot kill you as well.

rows.acip: ,GSON RKYEN RNAMS KYANG 'CHI RKYEN DU MA GYUR PA MED DE, MI 'CHI BA'I PHYIR DU NI BZA' BTUNG DANG GNAS KHANG DANG GROGS LA SOGS PA RNAMS TSOL LA, DE DAG KYANG BZA' BTUNG HA CANG MANGS PA DANG HA CANG NYUNGS PA DANG MI 'PHROD PA LONGS SPYAD PA SOGS DANG , GNAS KHANG RDIB PA DANG MDZA' BOS BSLUS PA LA SOGS PA'I SGO NAS 'CHI BA'I RKYEN DU 'GYUR BAS NA 'CHI BA'I RKYEN DU MA SONG BA'I GSON PA'I RKYEN MI SNANG NGO ,
rows.wylie: gson rkyen rnams kyang 'chi rkyen du ma gyur pa med de, mi 'chi ba'i phyir du ni bza' btung dang gnas khang dang grogs la sogs pa rnams tshol la, de dag kyang bza' btung ha cang mangs pa dang ha cang nyungs pa dang mi 'phrod pa longs spyad pa sogs dang , gnas khang rdib pa dang mdza' bos bslus pa la sogs pa'i sgo nas 'chi ba'i rkyen du 'gyur bas na 'chi ba'i rkyen du ma song ba'i gson pa'i rkyen mi snang ngo
rows.english: Beyond all this is the fact that there is nothing at all that we use to keep ourselves alive that cannot also turn into something that kills us. We spend our lives searching for food and drink, or a place to stay, or friends or the like, with the intent that they help keep us from dying. But they can all turn into something that kills us instead. If we eat or drink too much, or too little, or ingest something which is not clean or the like, it can kill us. Our house can collapse on us, and our friends can cheat us, and they can all in the end lead us to our deaths. You literally cannot find anything that is supposed to keep you alive that cannot kill you as well.

rows.wylie: sems can rnams ni gnas la dga' zhing yul rnams 'dod, ,'dzin la gnas shing mi mkhas blun rmongs mun pa bzhin, ,thob par bya ba'i chos ni gnas med 'dzin med de, ,des na 'jig rten dag dang rtsod pa 'byung ba yin, ,zhes dang
rows.english: The beings in this world Crave for a place to stay, And make nations for themselves. They live in grasping; They know not what they do— Fools, confused in the dark. But the place we want to go Is one nowhere, Where nothing can be grasped. Thus it is that disagreement Has arisen between Those of the world, and ourselves.
